dedupe_keys.name: waterway sim agent based inland waterway tow navigation model

description: waterway-sim is a NetLogo agent-based model of inland waterway tow traffic in the context of extreme weather events. It uses continuous safe-distance traffic logic and adds rules for navigating locks and dams, passing, one-way zones and bridge passage, with interface parameters for tow operation decisions during extreme weather that follow official Waterway Action Plan guidance. The waterway is drawn as a straight line with customisable river miles for locks, dams and bridges. The repository holds the model, an updated version and R scripts used to process simulation output in a validation study, which used Ohio River AIS barge data from 2013 and 2014 and was reported in Transportation Research Record in 2020; the original model was published in Transportation Research Record in 2017 by Nelson, Camp, Philip and Abkowitz. Coverage is generic, calibrated for a river such as the Ohio. Access: free on GitHub under CC BY-SA 4.0; it needs NetLogo 3D with the time, xw and csv extensions. Caveats: the author gives no accuracy guarantee outside the validated case, and the model ignores vessel, channel and hydrological characteristics. It supports disruption and resilience analysis of lock and river closures and operating policy tests, and complements the Mississippi and Arkansas inland waterway digital twin case catalogued here.
